turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll grab a few vitals before Dr. Alvarez comes in. Go ahead and have a seat.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Um, these cuffs always squeeze way too hard.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): They do. Let your arm go loose for me. Blood pressure is 138 over 86.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that bad? I don't know, doctor— sorry. You're the nurse.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): All good. It's a little up there for a clinic reading, nothing I'm paging anyone about. Pulse is 78. Temperature's 36.8.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I feel kind of warm, but I don't think I'm actually sick.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Oxygen is 98 percent. You're set. She'll be in shortly. The decent magazine's already gone, fair warning.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hey, sorry about the wait. I'm Dr. Alvarez. What's been going on?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, headaches. I've had them forever, but they're different now. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Different how? Say it however it comes out.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): They used to show up in the afternoon, kind of behind my eyes. Now I wake up with them. Worse in the morning, before I even get to the coffee.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has the morning part been happening?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe a month? Or six weeks? I'm terrible with dates.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): We don't need the exact day. The older headaches, how far back do those go?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Years. Since my thirties. I'm 47, so fifteen years? Something like that. My sister gets them too, but that's— never mind, not why I came.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): We can leave your sister aside. With these morning ones, any nausea, any vomiting?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. I threw up twice this week. Not every morning. Just sometimes, and then I feel completely wrung out.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the light bother you, or noise?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Light, yeah, same as always. I end up pulling the blinds. Noise not really.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): What are you taking when they hit?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan, the 50 milligram tablets. And Tylenol. Acetaminophen. I go through a lot of it.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many days a week on the sumatriptan?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Most days lately. Five, six days a week. The box says not to, I know, I know.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the Tylenol, how much at a time?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Extra strength, 500 milligrams, two of them, maybe three times a day. Sometimes more if it's a bad one. I don't know, doctor, I lose count by dinner.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else in the mix, prescriptions or otherwise?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Vitamin D, those little gel capsules. And I was on propranolol for the headaches, but I stopped. Last year, I think. It made me so tired I just quit.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Whoever booked you mentioned snoring, and that you've been tired. Your husband, I think.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, he fusses. I snore, sure, everybody does. And I'm tired because my head hurts, not— I don't know. It's nothing.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): So from what he hears, you do snore?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, he says I do. I never hear it. And yeah, I'm wiped out in the afternoons, but that's the headaches. He's blowing it up.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll put it down and we won't go hunting for a sleep problem today. Any weakness, numbness, trouble getting words out, or double vision?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or a stiff neck?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Neck's not stiff. It's the head, that's all.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any hit to the head lately? A fall?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I tripped over the dog last month, but I didn't hit my head. Dog's fine. He's a menace on the stairs.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Glad he's okay. Quick look, then. Follow my finger... good, your eyes move fully. Pupils are equal.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Am I supposed to look at the finger or at you? Sorry.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Finger's perfect. Squeeze both my hands... strength is even on the two sides. Walk over to the door for me... balance looks fine.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Did I pass? I felt clumsy, but these shoes are slippery.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): You did fine. Neuro exam is normal. No focal signs that I can find.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): So what do you think it is? I don't know, doctor, my brain goes straight to the scary stuff.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): What fits best is medication overuse stacked on the migraines you've had for years. The new morning pattern, with the vomiting, means I can't totally rule out something else underneath.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Like a tumor? Don't say tumor. Or say it, I don't know.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not saying tumor. The exam doesn't point that way. If this new pattern doesn't settle after we ease off the pain pills, we might do a head CT. I'm not ordering one today.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): So we just wait and see?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let's see how two weeks go. If the morning headaches and the vomiting haven't eased by then, come back and we'll set up the scan.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): And if they calm down I just stay home?
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Exactly, only if it's not better. In the meantime, keep sumatriptan to no more than two days in a week. Same with the Tylenol, try not to take it every single day.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know if I can do that when it's really pounding.

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): If one is truly awful, one 50 milligram sumatriptan is okay. Just not most days. Water, and a steadier bedtime, matter more than they sound. If you ever get a sudden worst headache of your life, weakness, confusion, or vomiting that will not stop, go to the ER.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I'll try. My husband is going to say I told you so, about the pills.
[SEG0054] person_1 (NURSE): I can hold a Thursday afternoon two weeks out, if you want it locked in before you leave.
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks, hold off on booking. If things haven't settled in two weeks, she can call and we'll see her, and talk about that CT.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): He also wanted me to ask about a sleep study. I don't know, doctor. I think he's overdoing it.
[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll leave sleep alone for now. No sleep study from me today. Anything else you wanted to cover?
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. The garage ate my parking ticket, but that's not medical. I think that's everything.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll take it a step at a time. Take care.

spec.situation: Person with long headaches who now has a different pattern (worse in the morning, or with vomiting); takes sumatriptan or paracetamol often; partner says snoring and tiredness too; patient dismisses it. Doctor does a quick neuro exam and orders a scan conditionally.
features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Snoring is reported by husband and acknowledged by patient; not solely patient-reported with certainty.

omissions.text: Patient feels completely wrung out after the episodes of vomiting/headache.
Prior headaches used to occur in the afternoon.
Acetaminophen entry is misleadingly recorded as dose=500 mg; patient actually takes extra-strength 500 mg tablets, 2 at a time (1000 mg per dose), maybe 3 times a day and sometimes more.
Propranolol was stopped because it made the patient very tired.
Patient denied hitting her head after tripping over the dog last month; there was a fall/trip without head impact.

Follow-up timing was specifically to see how two weeks go; if morning headaches and vomiting have not eased by then, patient should call/come back and CT will be arranged/discussed. No CT is being ordered today.
Doctor explicitly deferred sleep evaluation: no sleep study today / will leave sleep alone for now.
